name: On Holding
thesis: Currently trading at 36.06 aftermarket which represents a 9% gain for no apparent reason or news, shorting due to sudden jump.

name: SoftBank Group
thesis: Holding company whose value rests on its stakes in Arm, SoftBank Corp., the Vision Funds and OpenAI. Shares trade at a discount to the value of those assets after a c. 29% fall over the year. Further gains on its AI holdings, share buybacks and a narrowing of that discount could all lift the price. Key risks: high leverage and results driven by asset revaluations rather than operating profit.

name: Nu Holdings (Nubank)
thesis: Brazil's presidential runoff on 25 Oct, won by Lula against market expectations, triggered a sharp sell-off in Brazilian assets. Nu fell about 17% the next day and now trades well below its January high, at a much lower earnings multiple than its recent history. With most of its customers in Brazil, the stock was repriced on political risk rather than any change in the business, making this an attractive entry point. Long-term growth comes from continued customer growth and expansion in Mexico and Colombia. Key risks: Brazilian interest rates and fiscal policy, credit quality, and the currency.

name: MDA Space
thesis: Recent sell-off offers an attractive entry point: the shares trade roughly 40% below their 52-week high despite revenue growth above 20% and raised 2026 guidance. Net cash of about CAD 1.3bn funds expansion across North America and Europe through the acquisitions of Blue Canyon Technologies (US) and CLS (France). Key risks: a shrinking backlog, weak free cash flow and acquisition integration.

name: Wizz Air
thesis: Highly leveraged airline that has swung to a loss: operating profit fell 17% last year, interest is no longer covered by operating profit and current assets do not cover short-term liabilities. Ranked the weakest balance sheet in my screen. Key risks: strong passenger growth, relief on grounded engines and frequent short squeezes. Closed for now; I may come back to the trade depending on the oil price outlook.

name: American Airlines
thesis: Loss-making with negative shareholders' equity and very thin interest cover. Q3 posted a USD 269m net loss as fuel costs rose 67%, and management guides to a full-year loss. Key risks: revenue growing c. 20%, a fall in oil prices and high short interest (c. 15%) that could fuel a squeeze. Closed for now; I may come back to the trade depending on the oil price outlook.

name: Hyperliquid Strategies
thesis: Short-term rebound trade. The shares are trading about 8.7% below Friday's close ahead of the US open, a sharp move for a company whose value rests mainly on its holdings of the HYPE token. Expected to recover part of the fall once regular trading opens. Key risk: the share price follows the HYPE token, so further falls in crypto would push it lower.

name: Nvidia
thesis: AI sell-off ahead of the Anthropic IPO, which prices this week and will test investor appetite for AI. Jensen Huang's resignation as CEO leaves Nvidia under an interim CEO, while the company faces scrutiny over compliance with chip export controls. Shares are down about a quarter this month, with momentum still negative into Q3 results.

name: Micron Technology
thesis: AI sell-off ahead of the Anthropic IPO, which prices this week and will test investor appetite for AI. Memory makers are among the hardest hit as investors worry about a slowdown in the AI build-out, and the fallout from Jensen Huang's resignation at Nvidia weighs on the whole chip sector. Memory is a cyclical business priced near peak conditions.

name: IREN

name: Cipher Digital
thesis: AI sell-off ahead of the Anthropic IPO, which prices this week and will test investor appetite for AI. AI data-centre operators such as CoreWeave and Nebius are leading the decline on fears of a slower AI build-out. Loss-making and highly indebted after recent debt raises to fund its AI data-centre build-out.

name: Nvidia
thesis: Earnings trade. Q3 FY2027 results beat on every line: revenue of USD 115.8bn, up 103% year on year and well above the USD 108bn guidance and c. USD 109bn consensus; data-centre revenue of USD 107.6bn, up 110%; adjusted EPS of USD 2.68 vs USD 2.48 expected. Q4 revenue guided to c. USD 130bn, above the c. USD 125bn consensus, with Vera Rubin shipments under way. After a c. 24% fall this month, the beat should trigger a rebound. Key risks: CEO transition and export-control scrutiny.

thesis: Quick, highly leveraged trade: limit buy orders set to fill on the very high liquidity after Nvidia's earnings call, with Asian markets (Japan and China) expected to rally around these semiconductor stocks later in the evening.

name: Take-Two Interactive
thesis: Limit buy set to fill at 215.5, on the view that GTA VI hype would cool overnight after a 10% two-day pullback driven by the wider AI/tech selloff, then spike at the open as the launch approached. Catalysts: near-perfect early reviews (99 on Metacritic), pre-orders ahead of plan, record livestream audiences, and reiterated Buy ratings (Bank of America, Oppenheimer, Jefferies) ahead of the 19 November release.

name: Everpure
thesis: The whole market turned lower after strong gains at the open; Everpure, among the day's biggest gainers, is expected to give back its move.

name: Anthropic
thesis: Trading the volatility around Anthropic's first day of trading. The IPO was very hard to approach: priced at $83, the stock opened at $111.50 and spiked to about $115, roughly 34% above the offer, as buyers added valuation down to the last dime. End-of-day target around $96 (± $3). View: Anthropic may have used up in a single day the post-IPO momentum that SpaceX's listing built over two weeks, and early holders who bought far below the IPO price (such as buyers of the former FTX stake at about $30 a share) have strong reasons to take profits.

name: Intuit
thesis: Intuit fell about 13% in after-hours trading, mainly because it agreed to sell Mailchimp to Bending Spoons for about $3.68 billion, far below the roughly $12 billion it paid in 2021, alongside disappointing numbers and an analyst downgrade. Added pressure from AI competition: OpenAI launched ChatGPT for Accounting the day before, automating bookkeeping, reconciliations and month-end reports, a direct threat to QuickBooks' role. A very short, volatile trade capturing small moves, which is why it was leveraged: leverage was needed to exploit such a sharp market reaction.

name: Moderna
thesis: Rotation into defensive stocks: healthcare names such as Moderna were rising while the tech sell-off continued. A quick, highly leveraged trade on that move.

name: Mastercard
thesis: Rotation into defensive stocks while the tech sell-off continued: the AI sell-off is bringing money back into the defensive sector after its own sell-off earlier this week. A quick, leveraged trade on that move.

name: Palo Alto Networks
thesis: Bought the dip near the day's low (around $350) after a roughly 3% pullback with the tech sell-off, a few days after a strong fiscal Q1: revenue up 39% to $3.44 billion, raised full-year guidance and a wave of analyst price-target increases. Cybersecurity spending is less exposed to the AI-capex doubts hitting the sector, so a quick rebound was likely. Short, leveraged trade.

name: Mitsubishi Corp
thesis: Passes 6 of 8 balance-sheet and profitability tests: current ratio 1.5, debt/equity 0.65, interest cover 3.0x, net margin 5.1%, ROE 11.7% and strong free cash flow (about ¥1.6tn, a 9% FCF yield). P/E of 16.9 (14.6 forward) sits in the undervalued band. Strongest momentum of Japan's trading houses: first-half profit up 74% to ¥619.7bn, full-year target raised to a record ¥1.2tn and a buyback of up to ¥1tn. Risks: the most expensive of the group after a 35% rise in a year, and exposure to energy and metals prices.

name: Marubeni
thesis: Best scorecard among Japan's major trading houses, passing 7 of 8 tests: current ratio 1.4, debt/equity 0.57, interest cover 4.2x, net margin 6.2%, ROE 14.4% (highest of the group), ROA 5.5% and positive free cash flow (about a 6% FCF yield). P/E of 12.7 (11.3 forward) is firmly in the undervalued band, and analysts' average target is about 32% above the price. Risks: commodity-cycle exposure and net debt of about 3.7x EBITDA (overstated, as EBITDA excludes equity-method income).

name: HP Inc.
thesis: HP's better-than-expected fiscal Q4 results (revenue of $16.0bn, guidance in line to above estimates and a higher dividend) sent the stock up about 15% after hours to $32.03. After a spike that sharp in thin after-hours trading, a pullback looked very likely, so the trade was kept very short. HP still looks strong and may well be a good longer-term investment, but the market is grasping at any hope: Jensen Huang's reinstatement at Nvidia lifted some tech stocks by more than 20% before they gave much of it back the next day.
